question.problem:
Consider the set of matrices ${A,B,C},$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

 
If the set is linearly dependent, find the value of $\frac{{x}_{3}}{{x}_{2}}$ from a non-zero solution of ${x}_{1}A+{x}_{2}B+{x}_{3}C=O,$ where $O$ is the $2\times 2$ zero-matrix.

If the set is linearly dependent, find the value of $\dfrac{x_1}{x_2}$ from a non-zero solution of $x_1A+x_2B=O,$ where $O$ is the $2 \times 2$ zero-matrix.
current_example.worked_solution:
If the set is linearly dependent, then there exist $x_1,x_2$ not both zero such that 

$$
x_1A+x_2B=O.
$$

Otherwise, if $x_1 = x_2 = 0,$ the set is linearly independent.

Substituting the matrices $A$ and $B$ into the above equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 2 & -6\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & 0 \\ -2{x}_{1} & 4{x}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2} & 5{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2} & -6{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} & 5{x}_{2} \\ -2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & 4{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{2}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 4{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we consider the corresponding augmented matrix and reduce it to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 4 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+(-4){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & -18 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{8}{5}){R}_{2} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+\frac{18}{5}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. Therefore, we get the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 5{x}_{2}=0,\end{aligned}
$$

which has only the zero solution $x_1=x_2=0.$

Consequently, $\big\{A, B \big\}$ is linearly independent.
